newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian manufacturing still down - survey.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian manufacturing still down - survey.

text.p: Australian manufacturing was experiencing another difficult quarter, although there were now signs of improving conditions, a new survey on Tuesday showed.

The Australian Chamber of Manufactures (ACM) survey said companies reporting September quarter falls in sales, profits production, capacity utilisation and employment outnumbered those reporting rises for the sixth successive quarter.

"An increasing number of companies, particularly those with high export orientation or strong seasonal markets, are seeing some light at the end of the tunnel, but many others are still doing it very hard," ACM chief executive Allan Handberg said.
The survey said average capacity utilisation fell to 68.8 percent in the September quarter, compared to 72.6 percent in the June quarter. This was its lowest level for three years.
The survey said export trends also weakened with 29 percent of manufacturers reporting a fall in exports, apparently in response to the stronger Australian dollar.

However, nearly one in every three companies reported an increase in production. This compared with the 38 percent which made further production cuts and reflected a narrowing of the gap since the June quarter when 37 percent of companies cut production and 24 percent lifted production.
Handberg said the survey indicated that the slowdown in manufacturing had moderated and the industry was now heading back towards more positive trends.

"The ACM survey confirms that there was a lift in confidence following the federal budget and this is being reinforced by the seasonal stimulus," he said. "However, current trends are consistent with an annual growth rate of perhaps 2.4 percent, still significantly lower than the economy as a whole."
The survey found about 46 percent of the surveyed companies expected to increase production before Christmas with only 11 percent expecting further declines.
Export trends were also expected to recover with 39 percent of companies anticipating gains and only 10 percent expecting declines, the survey said.
However, it said intense competition continued to put pressure on selling prices with 23 percent reporting September quarter price cuts and only 15 percent reporting increases.
The survey also found profitability declined in all 12 manufacturing sectors with 46 percent reporting profit falls in the September quarter and 23 percent reporting rises.
The ACM survey covers 620 companies, making total annual sales of A$25 billion and employing a total of 92,000 people.
